t: Routines, programs and the main routine
html:
A program is a set of routines; one of them is the main routine and is the only one the controller scans on its own. Every other routine runs because a JSR(Name) in a running routine jumps to it, scans it top to bottom, and returns. A main routine made of nothing but JSRs is the cleanest way to organise a machine, and it is how Part IV is written:

JSR(S1_Run);
JSR(S2_Dwell);
JSR(S4_Registers);
JSR(S5_Fill);
JSR(S6_Supply);
JSR(S7_Cap);
JSR(S8_Sort);
JSR(S9_Count);
JSR(S10_Label);
JSR(S11_Alarms);
JSR(S12_Pack);
JSR(S14_Hazard);
JSR(S15_Inspect);
JSR(S13_Mix);
JSR(S3_Index);

Order matters, because of the scan. Step 3 (index the belt) is written early, because every station needs bottles to arrive, but its JSR is always the last one in MainRoutine: it is called after the registers, the fill, the cap, the label and the inspection (steps 4, 5, 7, 10 and 15) so that a request raised this scan is seen by the index logic in the same scan. Put the JSR for step 3 above step 5 and the belt can step before the request is noticed; the Try it in step 5 asks you to do exactly that and watch. Inside each routine the rungs are written top to bottom, and each one works the moment it is written; MainRoutine is the one place where the order is about the scan.

Logic → New Routine… (or right-click the program) adds a routine; a routine with no JSR to it is dead code. SBR and RET pass parameters to and from a routine; JMP(Label) and LBL(Label) skip rungs within one; AFI (always false) parks a rung you want to keep but not run; NOP is a placeholder. Structured Text routines are supported too (Help → Structured Text), and Add-On Instructions package logic with its own parameters as a reusable instruction, drawn as a box like TON (Help → Add-On Instructions).

Tasks

Programs run in tasks. MainTask is continuous and runs every 20 ms scan. Right-click Tasks → New Task… for another one, and right-click a program → Schedule In… to move it to a task.

  • Periodic runs once every period of machine time. A period shorter than the scan (5 ms, say) runs several times per scan; timers inside it count the time since the task last ran, so they keep real time at any period.
  • Event runs when an EVENT(TaskName) instruction fires, when its trigger tag goes true (or changes at all), or after its timeout if nothing triggered it. A light-curtain bit, a part-present sensor or a registration mark is the usual trigger.

Priority 1 is the highest and 15 the lowest; the continuous task is below all of them. Periodic and event tasks interrupt the continuous task between rungs, at the moment they come due, so a value the continuous task read on rung 2 can be different by rung 20. That is real controller behaviour, and the reason for UID() and UIE() around rungs whose data must stay consistent, and for CPS, the copy nothing can interrupt.

Watch for

An integer DIV, MOD or CPT by zero is a major fault: the scan stops at that rung, the outputs go off, the mode shows Faulted and the fault is written to Errors and the Simulator Log. Communications → Clear Faults returns to Program mode. If a program exists under Controller Fault Handler it runs once and the fault is cleared by itself, as a handler that clears the fault record does in Logix. A REAL destination gives ±infinity and a minor fault instead, and a result too big for its type wraps and logs a minor fault; the last five are in Controller Properties.
